Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

famous adjective

also well-known, well known, renowned, celebrated, famous for, be famous, fame

classical

Catull. 46.6: ad clārās Asiae volēmus urbēs
Quint. 1.1.36: dicta clārōrum virōrum

clārus, clāra, clārum

famous, renowned

First bright and clear, of light, and loud, of sound (see loud); then clear to the mind, and famous, with the ablative of what for. The superlative clārissimus was the standing title of senators and consuls (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • nōbilis, nōbile — well known, famous; of noble birth

    also used · classical · Plin. NH 4.116; Phaedr. App. 21.1: equum … multīs palmīs nōbilem

    From nōscō: known, and so famous, often with the ablative of what for (Traupman 204: famous for). Of people it usually means noble, of a family that has held high office (Lewis & Short).

  • celeber, celebris, celebre — much frequented; famous

    also used · classical · Ov. M. 3.339 (Lewis & Short); Tib. 2.1.33 (Lewis & Short)

    First crowded, much visited (locus celeber, a busy place); “famous” mostly from Augustan writers on (Lewis & Short). The verb celebrāre is to throng, and so to make famous: Tagus auriferīs harēnīs celebrātur (Plin. NH 4.115).

  • praeclārus, praeclāra, praeclārum — splendid, excellent, distinguished

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.7.7: praeclārīs operibus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 313

    Very fine, noble, remarkable; famous as a work of praise rather than of report.

  • inclutus, incluta, inclutum — renowned, glorious

    also used · classical · Verg. A. 6.479: inclutus armīs; Traupman 204

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Enn., Lucr., Verg., Hor.; not in Caesar or Cicero (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • ad clārās Asiae volēmus urbēs

    let’s fly to the famous cities of AsiaCatull. 46.6

  • oppida ā Tagō memorābilia in ōrā Olisīpō, equārum ē favōniō ventō conceptū nōbile

    the notable towns on the coast from the Tagus: Lisbon, famous for its mares conceived by the west windPlin. NH 4.116

  • etiam dicta clārōrum virōrum et ēlēctōs ex poētīs maximē … locōs ēdiscere inter lūsum licet

    even the sayings of famous men and passages chosen mostly from the poets can be learned by heart in playQuint. 1.1.36

See also loud, name, classic, praise.

SourcesLewis & Short: clarus · Lewis & Short: nobilis · Lewis & Short: celeber · Lewis & Short: celebro · Lewis & Short: praeclarus · Lewis & Short: inclutus
